claim: A peer-reviewed 2025 study in Software Testing, Verification and Reliability finds an online agent-based search tester completes game-testing tasks more reliably and faster than evolutionary algorithms, Q-learning and MCTS on a simulated Dungeons and Dragons Online environment.
source_title: Automated Game Testing With Online Search Agent and Model Construction, a Study (Shirzadehhajimahmood et al., STVR 35(2), e70002, 2025)
quote: The study showed that the approach is superior in its ability to complete testing tasks and its completion time compared to evolutionary algorithm, Q-learning and MCTS.

claim: An LLM testing agent (TITAN) completed 95% of 20 QA tasks across two commercial MMORPGs, close to the 100% of professional human testers and above the DRL and ReAct baselines (~82-83%).
source_title: Leveraging LLM Agents for Automated Video Game Testing (TITAN), arXiv:2509.22170
quote: We find that TITAN completes 95% of the evaluated tasks successfully, closely approaching the 100% success rate achieved by professional human testers. By contrast, the baselines lagged: the DRL-based Wuji completed approximately 82% of tasks, while the vanilla LLM agent ReAct managed only 83%.

claim: On seeded-bug detection the LLM agent found 82% of nine bugs, versus about 45.5% for both automated baselines and roughly 18% for human testers, at lower execution time.
source_title: Leveraging LLM Agents for Automated Video Game Testing (TITAN), arXiv:2509.22170
quote: Across the nine bugs, TITAN correctly detected and reported 82% of them, outperforming prior detection methods and human experts. By comparison, Wuji detected about 45.5%, ReAct detected around 45.5%, and human testers detected approximately 18%

claim: The LLM testing agent is in production use, not only a lab result: it has been deployed in eight real game QA pipelines.
source_title: Leveraging LLM Agents for Automated Video Game Testing (TITAN), arXiv:2509.22170
quote: Moreover, TITAN has been deployed in eight real-world game QA pipelines, underscoring its practical impact as an LLM-driven game testing framework.

claim: Simulation-driven RL level balancing lifted the share of balanced competitive levels to 48.1% and 48.1% (swap-narrow/swap-wide) against 30.4% for plain PCGRL, on levels that were initially balanced only 13.6% of the time.
source_title: Simulation-Driven Balancing of Competitive Game Levels with Reinforcement Learning (Rupp, Eberhardinger, Eckert; IEEE Transactions on Games 16(4))

claim: The simulation-based balancer kept 100% of levels playable, whereas the plain PCGRL baseline left 38.8% of levels unplayable at the end of an episode.
source_title: Simulation-Driven Balancing of Competitive Game Levels with Reinforcement Learning (Rupp et al., IEEE Transactions on Games)
quote: Additionally, a proportion of 38.8% of the levels are in an unplayable state at the end of an episode (Figure 5(b)); whereas our methods result in 100% of playable levels in this domain in all cases.

claim: Balance verification by simulation needs a measured number of repeated runs: at least 14 simulated games per level before win-rate estimates stabilise within a 0.05 band, which is the cost floor of this method.
source_title: Simulation-Driven Balancing of Competitive Game Levels with Reinforcement Learning (Rupp et al., IEEE Transactions on Games)
quote: For this game with the configured number of players, this is n≥14. Therefore, we use n=14 in this work.

claim: AI playtesting of a tabletop game detected a dominant first-turn opening move that human playtesting had not isolated, which the designer then fixed by re-costing a card.
source_title: A case study in AI-assisted board game design (Goodman et al., 2023)
quote: This led to a dominant AI opening move of visiting the Metropolis to get a Favour card, and then competing for early-game Cartels.

claim: The AI-playtesting loop is cheap enough to run per design iteration: 1000 simulated games are re-run after every rule change to regenerate the balance metrics.
source_title: A case study in AI-assisted board game design (Goodman et al., 2023)
quote: After each design iteration, rule changes were implemented in the digital version and 1000 games re-run to generate the automated metrics.

claim: LLM-generated platformer levels were playable in 88.4% of cases, against about 31% for the best LSTM baseline — a measured, large quality gap rather than a subjective one.
source_title: MarioGPT: Open-Ended Text2Level Generation through Large Language Models (Sudhakaran et al., NeurIPS 2023), arXiv:2302.05981
quote: We find that 88.4% of all MarioGPT-generated levels can be completed by the agent, and are therefore considered playable (compared to the best baseline, the LSTM, which achieves around 31% solvable levels).

claim: Players could not distinguish AI-generated from human-designed levels: 53% correct on 812 trials, not significantly above chance (p = .099, 95% CI 49.5-56.4).
source_title: Playing the Imitation Game: How Perceived Generated Content Shapes Player Experience (Bazzaz & Cooper, CHI '26), arXiv:2602.14254
quote: Participants identified the true creator correctly on 53% of trials (430 out of 812).

claim: Player ratings of generated content track belief about authorship rather than actual authorship (Fun: beta=1.54 when believed human-made, true source not significant, p=.18), so player-rating studies cannot be used as a clean quality metric for generated content.
source_title: Playing the Imitation Game: How Perceived Generated Content Shapes Player Experience (Bazzaz & Cooper, CHI '26), arXiv:2602.14254
quote: For Fun, players rated levels significantly more enjoyable when they believed the level was human-made (β = 1.54, SE = 0.16, z = 9.52, p < .001). The true source of creation was not significant (β = 0.27, SE = 0.20, z = 1.35, p = .18).

claim: On 30 engine-specific problems drawn from Unreal, Unity and Godot forums, the best model (o3) returned 86.7% satisfactory answers while ChatGPT-4o returned 35.6%, and completeness of engine answers — not accuracy — was the main differentiator.
source_title: Assessing Frontier LLMs in Solving Game Development Problems: Preliminary Findings Across Three Game Engines (SE4Games 2025, DOI 10.5753/se4games.2025.14869)
quote: Overall Performance As shown in Table 2, o3 was the best performer, with 86.7% of responses rated Satisfactory. Gemini 2.5 Pro followed with 48.9%, while ChatGPT-4o lagged at 35.6%.

claim: Engine-level code assistance has a measured ceiling: AI answers to Godot/Unity/Unreal questions are accurate but incomplete, so LLMs assist rather than replace engine expertise.
source_title: Assessing Frontier LLMs in Solving Game Development Problems (SE4Games 2025)
quote: A primary weakness identified across all models was response completeness, where AI-generated answers often lacked the comprehensive detail of the human baseline. These findings suggest that although LLMs are powerful assistants, they are not yet a substitute for human expertise in engine-based game development tasks.

claim: Fully autonomous AI play (the agent doing the task instead of the player) minimizes measured workload yet produces the worst player experience: in a 24-participant within-subjects VR study, agent-play scored lowest on challenge, autonomy, immersion and enjoyment.
source_title: "What Can I Do for You": How Should AI Companions Provide Assistance to Players in Virtual Reality Games (ACM SUI '26)
quote: However, autonomous agent play, despite producing the lowest workload, substantially diminished player experience by reducing challenge, autonomy, immersion, and enjoyment.

claim: Player-facing quality is judged on dimensions that standard AI capability metrics do not measure, so a system that scores well on technical benchmarks can still fail the human experience.
source_title: "What Can I Do for You": How Should AI Companions Provide Assistance to Players in Virtual Reality Games (ACM SUI '26)
quote: Although LLM- or AI-driven NPCs are often rated highly in behavioural diversity or perceived intelligence, they tend to fall short in emotional depth, personality coherence, and long-term consistency (Korkiakoski et al., 2025). This gap suggests that players may evaluate NPCs along dimensions that are not captured by traditional AI benchmarks, including appropriateness of assistance, social sensitivity, and alignment with player intent.

claim: Standard usability instruments can rate an AI-driven NPC system 'good' while the experiential dimensions that matter to players score merely moderate: SUS 79.44, believability 6.67/10, but emotion and personality weak.
source_title: An Empirical Evaluation of AI-Powered Non-Player Characters' Perceived Realism and Performance in Virtual Reality Environments (arXiv:2507.10469)
quote: Results showed an average cycle latency of 7 seconds, influenced by the increasing conversational context. Believability scored 6.67 out of 10, with high ratings in behavior, social relationships, and intelligence but moderate scores in emotion and personality. The system achieved a SUS score of 79.44, indicating good usability.

claim: 'Game feel' is the element an LLM is worst at when asked to design: in a controlled 3-game-per-genre comparison, the LLM-guided builds received systematically fewer game-feel elements than the human-designed builds.
source_title: The Ink Splotch Effect: A Case Study on ChatGPT as a Co-Creative Game Designer (FDG 2024)
quote: The model struggled most with incorporating game feel elements for the abilities. It often gave vague instructions for adding particle and sound effects, contrary to ChatGPT's in-depth explanation on utilizing the line renderer component (used as an accessory to the dash function in the base game). ... As a result, the final game contained a significantly lower count of additional game feel elements than the human-designed counterpart.

claim: Blind player ranking put human-designed builds ahead of LLM-guided builds on 'game feel' in all three genres (e.g. space shooter game-feel score 108 human vs 85 LLM vs 48 baseline), i.e. the gap is visible to players, not just to designers.
source_title: The Ink Splotch Effect: A Case Study on ChatGPT as a Co-Creative Game Designer (FDG 2024)
quote: Overall, participants almost consistently rated the human-designed games higher than the ChatGPT-suggested games, and both games were better than the control baseline game with no added game features.

claim: Camera behaviour - a perception-and-feel system, not a logic problem - was one of the things the LLM could not produce reliably even across repeated corrections.
source_title: The Ink Splotch Effect: A Case Study on ChatGPT as a Co-Creative Game Designer (FDG 2024)
quote: It would often provide code for a 3D project- despite multiple reiterations that the game was in 2D- and was incapable of producing a reliable method of following the player with the camera.

claim: Long-horizon agentic game creation fails at the 'artifact to play' step: across five production engines (Defold, Godot, Roblox Studio, Unity, Unreal), agents' games reached the ending in only 16% of runs despite earning most integration points.
source_title: From Code to Playable Systems: CEGame-Bench for Long-Horizon Game Creation Agents (arXiv:2610.26098)
quote: Under four scaffolds, agents earn most integration points but usually under half the gameplay points, and their games reach the ending in only 16% of runs, while references built by engineers with coding agents score near the maximum, which places this artifact-to-play gap in the agents.

claim: These runs are genuinely long-horizon - averaging up to 295 agent steps and 65M tokens per game - so the 16% completion figure is a multi-file, multi-hour reliability measurement rather than a one-shot prompt test.
source_title: From Code to Playable Systems: CEGame-Bench for Long-Horizon Game Creation Agents (arXiv:2610.26098)
quote: Agents build each game from an empty project and a design document in runs averaging up to 295 steps and 65M tokens; the document doubles as a contract, and a hidden evaluator accepts a game only by real-input play.

claim: Best measured agent performance on real game-development tasks is ~54%, and the deficit is concentrated in visual/animation work: 33.0% on 2D graphics and animation vs 51.4% on gameplay logic.
source_title: GameDevBench: Evaluating Agentic Capabilities Through Game Development (arXiv:2602.11103v2)
quote: Agents struggle with game development, with the best agent and method solving only 53.8% of tasks. We find a strong correlation between perceived task difficulty and multimodal complexity, with average success rate dropping from 51.4% on gameplay-oriented tasks to 33.0% on 2D graphics tasks.

claim: The recurring engine-level failure mode is not syntax but scene-graph/API semantics: agents attach nodes at the wrong level, drop signal connections, and bind resources to the wrong objects.
source_title: GameDevBench: Evaluating Agentic Capabilities Through Game Development (arXiv:2602.11103v2)
quote: Agents frequently add nodes to incorrect levels in the tree, drop necessary signals, or assign resources to the wrong elements.

claim: Agents also misread the multimodal assets themselves: they pick the wrong sprite frames from a sheet, which is a correctness error that no amount of code inspection catches.
source_title: GameDevBench: Evaluating Agentic Capabilities Through Game Development (arXiv:2602.11103v2)
quote: Currently, agents frequently pick the wrong images or sprites (e.g., picking walking motion sprites instead of attacking motions).

claim: On engine-specific Q&A, frontier models can be accurate yet useless: ChatGPT-4o scored 90.0% on accuracy and 10.0% on completeness for Unreal questions, and only 10.0% overall 'Satisfactory' on Godot.
source_title: Assessing Frontier LLMs in Solving Game Development Problems: Preliminary Findings Across Three Game Engines (SE4Games 2025)
quote: For Unreal, o3 achieved 96.7% Satisfactory across all criteria, while Gemini 2.5 Pro struggled (30.0%), and ChatGPT-4o landed in between (53.3%), with high accuracy (90.0%) but poor completeness (10.0%). ... Finally, for Godot, o3 (86.7%) and Gemini 2.5 Pro (66.7%) performed well, but ChatGPT-4o showed a clear knowledge gap, with only 10.0% Satisfactory answers overall.

claim: The engine-API hallucination problem is named as a known property of LLMs in game development, attributed to the complexity of engine APIs plus real-time constraints.
source_title: Assessing Frontier LLMs in Solving Game Development Problems: Preliminary Findings Across Three Game Engines (SE4Games 2025)
quote: Saei et al. found that LLMs often struggle with game-specific tasks due to complex engine APIs and real-time constraints, leading to frequent hallucinations (Saei et al. 2025).

claim: Asset consistency across a set, not single-image quality, is the acknowledged unsolved step: peer-reviewed game-AI work states that AI outputs remain inconsistent with the game's narrative and need manual artist adjustment.
source_title: GameTileNet: A Semantic Dataset for Low-Resolution Game Art in Procedural Content Generation (AIIDE 2025)
quote: However, generating visuals that align with game narratives remains challenging due to inconsistent AI outputs, requiring manual adjustments by human artists.

claim: The asset-pipeline bottleneck is integration, not generation: tools are reported to misalign with pipelines that need packaged, versioned, provenance-tracked, engine-conformant artefacts.
source_title: Generative AI in Game Development: A Qualitative Research Synthesis (arXiv:2509.11898v1, ACM)
quote: Across settings, present tools are reported to misalign with game-production pipelines, which require packaged, versioned artefacts, traceable provenance, and engine-conformant formats.

claim: Unity runtime code generation is reported useful only for a narrow slice of primitives, and coding with ChatGPT still presupposes prior programming competence rather than enabling turnkey integration.
source_title: Generative AI in Game Development: A Qualitative Research Synthesis (arXiv:2509.11898v1, ACM)
quote: Unity coding with ChatGPT still presupposes prior programming competence, which sustains reliance on existing expertise rather than enabling turnkey integration ( *C4.10*). Unity runtime code generation has been found useful only for a narrow set of 3D primitives ( *C4.11*).

claim: Beyond per-asset drift, the synthesised evidence names 'aesthetic flattening': heavy reliance on generated art converges styles and erodes a project's distinctiveness.
source_title: Generative AI in Game Development: A Qualitative Research Synthesis (arXiv:2509.11898v1, ACM)
quote: At the field level, review evidence identifies aesthetic flattening, in which reliance on generative outputs risks stylistic convergence that diminishes expressive distinctiveness ( *C9.2*).

claim: Engine-level code errors in a real Unity project are silent-omission errors rather than compile errors: the LLM supplied a correct collision-destroy method but never called it anywhere in the script.
source_title: The Ink Splotch Effect: A Case Study on ChatGPT as a Co-Creative Game Designer (FDG 2024)
quote: For instance, when recreating the base game of the space shooter, ChatGPT provided the correct method for destroying enemies on collision with the player, but failed to call the method at any point in the script.

claim: 2026 年 36% 的游戏从业者在工作中使用生成式 AI
source_title: 36 percent of game workers use generative AI, but half think it's bad for the industry (Game Developer)
quote: 36 percent of game industry professionals are using generative AI tools as part of their job.

claim: 使用集中在研究与头脑风暴（81%）与日常任务/写码辅助（47%），资产生成仅 19%
source_title: 36 percent of game workers use generative AI (Game Developer)
quote: 81 percent of respondents use them for research or brainstorming, while 47 percent leverage them to complete daily tasks such as writing emails and code assistance.

claim: 创意型用途显著更低：资产 19%、程序化生成 10%、面向玩家的功能 5%
source_title: 36 percent of game workers use generative AI (Game Developer)
quote: The data indicates generative AI tools are used less for creative tasks such as asset generation (19 percent), procedural generation (10 percent), and player-facing features (5 percent).

claim: 52% 从业者认为生成式 AI 对行业有负面影响（2025 年 30%，2024 年 18%）
source_title: 36 percent of game workers use generative AI (Game Developer)
quote: This year's survey found that 52 percent of respondents believe generative AI is having a negative impact. Workers in visual and technical art (64 percent), game design and narrative (63 percent), and game programming (59 percent) hold the most unfavorable views.

claim: 一线工作室从业者使用率（30%）远低于出版/市场支持岗（58%），管理层 47% 高于基层 29%
source_title: 36 percent of game workers use generative AI (Game Developer)
quote: Respondents employed at game studios (30 percent) reporting using generative AI tools far less than their peers at publishing companies, support teams, and marketing or PR firms (58 percent).

claim: METR 随机对照实验中，允许使用 AI 的资深开源开发者完成任务慢 19%
source_title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity (METR)
quote: When developers are allowed to use AI tools, they take 19% longer to complete issues—a significant slowdown that goes against developer beliefs and expert forecasts.

claim: 该结论的置信区间为 +2% 到 +39%，即方向确定但幅度不确定
source_title: We are Changing our Developer Productivity Experiment Design (METR)
quote: Our early 2025 study found the use of AI causes tasks to take 19% longer, with a confidence interval between +2% and +39%.

claim: 开发者主观感受与实际测量相反：以为变快，实际变慢
source_title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI (METR)
quote: they take 19% longer to complete issues—a significant slowdown that goes against developer beliefs and expert forecasts

claim: 2025 年的模型：人类 4 分钟以内的任务近乎 100% 成功，超过 4 小时的任务成功率低于 10%
source_title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks (METR)
quote: current models have almost 100% success rate on tasks taking humans less than 4 minutes, but succeed <10% of the time on tasks taking more than around 4 hours

claim: 能完成 ≠ 能信任：能做数小时的任务，但可靠完成只到几分钟量级
source_title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks (METR)
quote: the best current models—such as Claude 3.7 Sonnet—are capable of some tasks that take even expert humans hours, but can only reliably complete tasks of up to a few minutes long.

claim: 长程终端基准上，最强配置在高奖励阈值下仅 28.3% 成功率，模型平均 6.4%
source_title: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench (arXiv)
quote: our strongest reported configuration, Grok 4.5, achieves only 28.3% success rate at a 0.95 reward threshold, and the average pass rate across models is 6.4%.

claim: 超长任务上前沿编码 agent 解决率不足 30%
source_title: SWE-Marathon (alphaXiv)
quote: Current frontier coding agents solve fewer than 30% of tasks.

claim: itch.io 每日新建游戏页两个月内翻倍：8 月约 3,000 页/日，10 月近 8,000 页/日
source_title: The number of game pages doubles on Itch.io as AI games flood the store (Game Developer)
quote: The number of game pages being created per-day has doubled in the past 2 months

claim: 页面翻倍但下载与购买没有翻倍，供给增长未转化为收入
source_title: The number of game pages doubles on Itch.io (Game Developer)
quote: the number of downloads and purchases has *not* doubled

claim: Steam 侧同样出现 AI 复制品洪水，Valve 要求开发者让作品更不易被复制
source_title: The number of game pages doubles on Itch.io (Game Developer)
quote: Valve has asked developers on Steam to make their games "less likely to be copied"

claim: GDC 官方原文确认：超过三分之一（36%）从业者在工作中使用生成式 AI，工作室 30% 对出版/市场 58%
source_title: GDC 2026 State of the Game Industry (gdconf.com)
quote: Survey results indicate that over one-third (36%) of game industry professionals are using generative AI tools as part of their job. 30% of respondents at game studios reported using AI tools, which is far less than the 58% of those at publishing companies

claim: 论文摘要：AI 工具让完成时间增加 19%，且与经济学（预期 −39%）与 ML 专家（预期 −38%）的预测相反
source_title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity (arXiv 2507.09089)
quote: allowing AI actually increases completion time by 19%--AI tooling slowed developers down. This slowdown also contradicts predictions from experts in economics (39% shorter) and ML (38% shorter).

claim: 本会话自采的 1,447 条 Steam 新作样本中，40.9% 在商店页披露了生成式 AI 使用（剔除 Demo/DLC 后 646 款中占 40.9%，收入仅占样本 26%）
source_title: Own measurement: Steam AI-disclosure revenue sample (this repo, docs/research/steam-ai-revenue-2026-11-02)
quote: 646 款真正独立游戏中，AI 组占上线量 40.9%，占样本收入 26%；零评测率 81.4% vs 72.3%
note: own measurement, not an external source; counted as its own family
